newsitem.title: USA: South Dakota winter wheat hurt by freeze.
newsitem.headline: South Dakota winter wheat hurt by freeze.

text.p: Nearly one-third of South Dakota's winter wheat acreage was in poor to very poor condition in the week ended April 27, the State Agricultural Statistics Service said.
"Winter freeze damage for winter wheat was rated at 26 percent none, 26 percent light, 22 percent moderate, and 26 percent severe," the agency said in its weekly crop report.
Freeze damage to winter rye was rated 17 percent moderate, 43 percent light and 40 percent none.
Statewide, 81 percent of winter wheat and 85 percent of winter rye have broken dormancy, the agency said.

Seeding of spring wheat was only two percent complete, down 42 points from the five-year average and compared to 30 percent planted a year ago. Oats were five percent planted, far behind the average pace.
Winter wheat was rated in 41 percent good to excellent condition, 28 fair, 21 poor and 10 very poor. Winter rye was rated 54 percent good to excellent, 33 percent fair.
Livestock condition was rated 59 percent good to excellent, 33 fair, seven poor and one very poor.
Topsoil and subsoil moisture were both rated 60 percent surplus, 40 adequate, down slightly from a week ago.
